title: Advanced gate-level glitch modeling using ANNs
problem: Multiple Input Switching (MIS) effects induce undesired glitch pulses at CMOS gate outputs, potentially causing circuit malfunction and excessive power consumption. Accurate and efficient gate-level glitch modeling is essential but computationally expensive.
motivation: Glitch modeling is crucial for designing high-performance, low-power, and reliable integrated circuits.
method: The approach trains neural networks (machine learning models that learn patterns from examples) to predict what happens when multiple inputs to a circuit gate switch at nearly the same time: specifically, it calculates the shape of unwanted voltage spikes that appear, how much delay occurs as signals pass through, and how much power is wasted. Different neural network designs are tested to find the right balance between using less computer memory and keeping predictions accurate, and the trained models are then built into standard cell libraries that circuit designers use.
key_novelty: Instead of running expensive circuit simulations (SPICE) each time to predict glitches in gate designs, this approach uses trained neural networks to make the same predictions with comparable accuracy while using significantly less memory.
contributions: ML-based methodology for accurate gate-level glitch modeling under MIS conditions
Systematic evaluation of different ANN architectures for glitch characterization
Practical integration workflow for deploying ANNs in standard cell libraries
Achieves 2.19% average error versus SPICE simulation with minimal memory overhead
